claims.claim: Nvidia shipped CUDA Toolkit 13.5 on Wednesday, moving Vera Rubin from early developer access to general availability, alongside Linux driver 620.70.06.
claims.episode_span: Nvidia on Wednesday shipped CUDA Toolkit 13.5, moving the Vera Rubin platform from early developer access to general availability
claims.source_title: Nvidia CUDA 13.5 Goes Live With Full Vera Rubin Support for Production AI
claims.supporting_quote: Nvidia on Wednesday shipped CUDA 13.5, moving its Vera Rubin computing platform out of early developer access and into general availability, a step that lets enterprise customers put the hardware into production deployments. The release landed alongside the company's 620.70.06 Linux driver.

claims.claim: Nvidia said in June 2026 that Vera Rubin systems would pack up to 144 GPUs per rack and deliver more than 7 exaflops of AI-for-science throughput and 5 petaflops of native FP64.

claims.supporting_quote: Nvidia said in June 2026 that Vera Rubin systems would pack up to 144 GPUs per rack and deliver more than 7 exaflops of AI-for-science throughput and 5 petaflops of native FP64 performance.

claims.claim: Rubin and later GPUs no longer support Tesla Compute Cluster mode.

claims.supporting_quote: Rubin and later GPUs now support the Windows Display Driver Model and Microsoft Compute Driver Model but no longer support Tesla Compute Cluster mode, so applications and deployment scripts built around TCC will need reworking.

claims.claim: UCIe advanced packaging targets reach of 2 mm or less, up to 64 GT/s per pin, 64 lanes, and 0.25 pJ/bit unterminated, while standard packaging targets up to 25 mm, 16 to 32 GT/s, 16 lanes, and 0.5 pJ/bit with 50-ohm terminations.
claims.episode_span: energy target is 0.25 picojoules per bit
claims.source_title: A System-Level Approach To Protecting 3D-IC Signal Integrity
claims.supporting_quote: Advanced packaging (2.5D interposer/bridge): Optimizes for ultra-short reach (<=2 mm) at up to 64 GT/s per pin (UCIe 3.0), utilizing 64 single-ended mainband data lanes per module. It routes signals unterminated at the receiver to hit an ultra-dense energy efficiency of 0.25 pJ/bit.
